source_text: Καὶ γὰρ ἐγώ, μαθὼν περίβλημα πονηρὸν εἰς ἀποστροφὴν τῶν ἄλλων ἀνθρώπων περιτεθειμένον ὑπὸ τῶν φαύλων δαιμόνων τοῖς Χριστιανῶν θείοις διδάγμασι, καὶ ψευδολογουμένων ταῦτα καὶ τοῦ περιβλήματος κατεγέλασα καὶ τῆς παρὰ τοῖς πολλοῖς δόξης. Χριστιανὸς εὑρεθῆναι καὶ εὐχόμενος καὶ παμμάχως ἀγωνιζόμενος ὁμολογῶ, οἰχ ὅτι ἀλλότριά ἐστι τὰ Πλάτωνος διδάγματα τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ἀλλ᾿ ὅτι οὐκ ἔστι πάντη ὅμοια, ὥσπερ οὐδὲ τὰ τῶν ἄλλων, Στωϊκῶν τε καὶ ποιητῶν καὶ συγγραφέων. Ἕκαστος γάρ τις ἀπὸ μέρους τοῦ σπερματικοῦ θείου λόγου τὸ συγγενὲς ὁρῶν καλῶς ἐφθέγξατο· οἱ δὲ τἀναντία ἑαυτοῖς ἐν κυριωτέροις εἰρηκότες οὐκ ἐπιστήμην τὴν ἄπτωτον καὶ γνῶσιν τὴν ἀνέλεγκτον φαίνονται ἐσχηκέναι. Ὅσα οὖν παρὰ καλῶς εἴρηται, ἡμῶν τᾶν Χριστιανῶν ἐστι· τὸν γὰρ ἀπὸ ἀγεννήτου καὶ ἀῤῥήτου θεοῦ λόγον μετὰ τὸν θεὸν προσκυνοῦμεν καὶ ἀγαπῶμεν, ἐπειδὴ καὶ δι᾿ ἡμᾶς ἄνθρωπος γέγονεν, ὅπως καὶ τῶν παθῶν τῶν ἡμετέρων συμμέτοχος γενόμενος καὶ ἴασιν ποιήσηται. Οἱ γὰρ συγγραφεῖς πάντες διὰ τῆς ἐνούσης ἐμφύτου τοῦ λόγου σπορᾶς ἀμυδρῶς ἐδύναντο ὁρᾶν τὰ ὄντα. Ἕτερον γάρ ἐστι σπέρμα τινὸς καὶ μίμημα κατὰ δύναμιν δοθέν, καὶ ἕτερον αὐτό, οὗ κατὰ χάριν τὴν ἀπ᾿ ἐκείνου ἡ μετουσία καὶ μίμησις γίνεται.
thought_title: The seed of the Word and the whole Word
orientation: Justin is speaking in his own voice, explaining why he became a Christian and how Christian teaching relates to Greek philosophy.
pass_a_gloss: For I too, having learned that a wicked covering had been placed around the divine teachings of the Christians by the base demons for the turning away of other people, and that these things were being falsely spoken, I laughed at both the covering and the opinion among the many. I confess that I both pray and struggle with all my might to be found a Christian, not because the teachings of Plato are alien to those of Christ, but because they are not in every way similar, just as neither are those of the others, of the Stoics and poets and historians. For each one spoke well seeing what is akin from a part of the seed of the divine Word; but those who have said things contrary to themselves in more important matters are shown not to have had unerring knowledge and irrefutable understanding. Therefore whatever things have been said well belong to us Christians; for after God we worship and love the Word from the unbegotten and ineffable God, since also for our sake he became human, so that having become a partaker of our sufferings he might also bring about healing. For all the writers through the seed of the Word that was in them were able dimly to see the things that are. For one thing is the seed of something and an imitation given according to ability, and another thing is that very thing itself, of which the participation and imitation come about according to the grace from that one.

lemmas.gloss: with all one's might, in full contest

choices.why: Keeps the metaphor of something wrapped around the teachings; 'covering' preserves the concrete image of περίβλημα.
παμμάχως is an adverb of full contest; 'struggling with all my might' conveys the intensity of the athletic metaphor.
συγγενές means what is related or kindred; 'what is akin' keeps the kinship sense of the seed of the Word.

choices.term: ἐπιστήμην τὴν ἄπτωτον καὶ γνῶσιν τὴν ἀνέλεγκτον
choices.why: ἄπτωτος means not falling, hence unerring; ἀνέλεγκτος means not subject to refutation; the pair is rendered distinctly.

choices.english: from the unbegotten and ineffable God
choices.why: Uses the fixed glossary terms 'unbegotten' for ἀγέννητος; 'ineffable' for ἄῤῥητος preserves the sense of unutterable.
rejected: from the uncreated and unnameable God
from the ingenerate and unspeakable God

choices.why: συμμέτοχος means sharing in with; 'partaker' conveys participation in our sufferings.

pass_b_english: I too once learned that wicked demons had wrapped a slanderous covering around the divine teachings of Christians to turn other people away, and that they were spreading lies about these teachings. So I laughed at that covering and at the opinion held by the many.

I confess that I both pray and struggle with all my might to be found a Christian. Not because Plato's teachings are foreign to Christ's, but because they are not entirely like his, just as the teachings of the others are not either, whether Stoics, poets, or historians.

For each of them spoke well when he saw what is akin from a part of the seed of the divine Word. But those who have contradicted themselves in more important matters clearly did not possess unerring knowledge and irrefutable understanding.

Whatever has been said well by anyone belongs to us Christians. For after God we worship and love the Word who comes from the unbegotten and ineffable God, since he also became human for our sake, so that having become a partaker of our sufferings he might also bring healing.

For all the writers were able to see reality only dimly through the seed of the Word that was in them. For the seed of something and an imitation given according to one's capacity are one thing, and the very reality itself is another, from which the participation and imitation come by his grace.
